title: Airlifts
hookLine: Operation Magic Carpet brings Yemenite Jews; Operation Solomon brings Ethiopian Jews

cards: An airfield in Aden, heat shimmering off the runway. Families who have come from villages across Yemen sit near a propeller plane with their bundles.

Some of them, the story goes, have never stood this close to an airplane. An old man, as it's told, looks up at the silver wings and says the Torah already spoke of this: God bore our ancestors on eagles' wings.

teach.b: The words he meant are in Exodus.
At Mount Sinai, before the commandments, God tells Moses to say to the people: "Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles' wings, and brought you unto Myself."
The airlift from Yemen became known around the world as Operation Magic Carpet, and its official name, people say, came straight from that verse: On Wings of Eagles. Years later came another.
Operation Solomon carried Ethiopian Jews, the Beta Israel, out of Addis Ababa while a civil war closed in, plane after plane.
Two airlifts, two very different communities, the same old picture of being carried. Now look closer at the verse. Rashi, the medieval commentator, asks why an eagle.
Other birds, he says, carry their young between their feet, because they fear the birds flying above them.
The eagle carries its young on its wings, because it fears only the arrow from below, and it would rather the arrow strike itself than its children. So the picture is not just speed.
It's a parent's body between the child and the danger.
And notice where the verse ends: not on a map, but "unto Myself." The journey's goal is closeness.
This week walked a long road: never again, whoever the neighbor is; choosing life; two memories of one year; the camps for displaced persons; the Mizrahi families who left; many exiles meeting.
Today, the wings that carried some of them home.

how: Exodus 19:4, 'I bore you on eagles' wings', is read in synagogue in the Torah portion Yitro, and Yemenite and Ethiopian Jewish families retell the airlifts that brought them to Israel.

games.q: you are an old man at an airfield in Aden. you have never flown. the plane is loud and strange. what do you do?
o: refuse to board and turn back.
board, calling it the eagles' wings of the Torah.
wait for some other way to travel.
games.why: the story often told is that Yemenite Jews boarded seeing the planes as the eagles' wings of Exodus.

practice: Bring to mind a journey that carried you, or someone you love, somewhere new: a move, a flight, a long drive in the dark. Who held the tickets, the baby, the bags?
Picture that journey from high above, small and brave, and if you pray, say the verse's words, on eagles' wings, in thanks for one person who carried you.

wordCard.voice: Airlifts. Operation Magic Carpet and Operation Solomon, which flew Yemenite and Ethiopian Jews to Israel. The last word of this week.
